newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SALO LEADS ISLES TO THIRD STRAIGHT 2-0 WIN OVER CAPS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SALO LEADS ISLES TO THIRD STRAIGHT 2-0 WIN OVER CAPS.

text.p: New York Islanders goalie Tommy Salo has the Washington Capitals' number. It's 2-0.
Salo stopped 39 shots Sunday for his fourth shutout of the season -- and his third straight by a 2-0 score against Washington.
"Today, when there was five minutes left, I started thinking it would be fun to have three shutouts against this team," Salo said.
"Tommy played unbelievable and when Tommy plays unbelievable, we win," said Islanders defenceman Rich Pilon.
Marty McInnis and Claude Lapointe scored for the Isles as the Caps got caught in another kind of numbers game as well as the 2-0 syndrome.

Washington was undermanned, since the Capitals traded forwards Anson Carter and Jason Allison and goaltender Jim Carey to the Boston Bruins on Saturday for centre Adam Oates, right wing Rick Tocchet and goaltender Bill Ranford.

Only Ranford was available, and he sat out as Olaf Kolzig started in goal. Tocchet asked for one or two more days to allow his sore ankle to heal and Oates begged out via his agent, according to Capitals general manager David Poile.
"There's no question that his contract is part of the reason why he's not here today," Poile said before the game.
"It's fair to say that he has gone through pretty much of an emotional roller coaster in the last week or so. I do not know the situation as to when Adam Oates will be arriving in Washington."

Salo has stopped all 96 shots he has faced against Washington this season. He made 11 saves in each of the first two periods and 17 in the third to help the Islanders snap a 1-4 slide and go 4-0 against Washington this season, outscoring the Caps 12-1.
The Capitals dropped to 1-5-1 in their last seven games.

The Islanders moved out of last place in the Eastern Conference and got within five points of the Tampa Bay Lightning and Hartford Whalers for the eighth and final playoff spot in the East. They are three points behind the Caps, who are tie for 10th with the Ottawa Senators.
"It's a game we had to win," said Islanders coach Rick Bowness. "We had to get something out of today's game, there's absolutely no question about that. We've been good enough to stay in the hunt."
In Hartford, Garth Snow made 26 saves to extend his personal unbeaten streak to 16 games and John LeClair had a goal and two assists to lead the Philadelphia Flyers to a 5-2 victory over the Whalers.

Snow is 11-0-5 since stopping an 0-5-1 slide on November 26. He made seven saves in the first period, six in the second and 13 in the third as the Flyers improved to 4-0-1 in their last five games and 7-1-2 in their last 10.

The Flyers are in first place in the Eastern Conference and have an eight-point lead over the New Jersey Devils and Buffalo Sabres. They rebounded from a 5-5 tie in Boston on Saturday in which they allowed a pair of late goals and played sub-par in overtime.
In Detroit, Ted Drury scored with 9:51 left in the third period to lift the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim into a 1-1 tie with the Red Wings, who extended their season-high unbeaten streak to eight games.

Kevin Todd passed the puck to Drury at the top of the right faceoff circle and skated toward the top of the crease. Drury skated to the bottom of the right circle and flipped a backhander past goaltender Mike Vernon, who was screened by Todd.
Kirk Maltby had scored at 4:22 of the third quarter to break a scoreless tie.
Vernon made 24 saves for Detroit, 5-0-3 in its last eight games. Each team had only one shot on goal in overtime.
Guy Hebert stopped 34 shots for the Mighty Ducks, who are 4-0-2 in their last six games. Anaheim is just 1-9-4 all-time against Detroit.
In Phoenix, Jeff Hackett turned aside 38 shots en route to his second shutout in his last seven games and sixth of his career as the Chicago Blackhawks defeated the Coyotes 4-0.
Brent Sutter had a pair of goals for the Blackhawks, 9-4-1 in their last 14 games. Chicago also raised its record to 6-3-1 in its last 10 road games.
Alexei Zhamnov and Tony Amonte both scored short-handed goals for Chicago.
Phoenix managed a season-high 23 shots in the second period but lost for the fourth time in its last five games.
